description: Step 8: the context the RAG hands the Arbiter and its first answers; the named-card search and the retriever's cut moved, so every ranking should stay the same

metrics.name: Recall@10
metrics.what: Out of the chunks a question needs, the share found in the first 10.
metrics.how: The chunks a question needs are the ones its answer key cites. Count how many of them are ranked 1 to 10, then divide by how many there are: 3 found out of 4 gives 75%. Then take the average over all the questions.
metrics.represents: Whether the first 10 chunks hold what the answer needs, in any order: a needed chunk counts as much at rank 10 as at rank 1, and not at all at rank 11.

metrics.name: Recall@20
metrics.what: Out of the chunks a question needs, the share found in the first 20.
metrics.how: The chunks a question needs are the ones its answer key cites. Count how many of them are ranked 1 to 20, then divide by how many there are: 3 found out of 4 gives 75%. Then take the average over all the questions.
metrics.represents: Whether the first 20 chunks hold what the answer needs, in any order: a needed chunk counts as much at rank 20 as at rank 1, and not at all at rank 21.

metrics.name: Binary nDCG@10
metrics.what: How close to the top the needed chunks are, in the first 10. From 0 to 1.
metrics.how: Each needed chunk in the first 10 earns points, fewer the lower it sits: 1 at rank 1, 0.63 at rank 2, 0.5 at rank 3, 0.29 at rank 10. The formula is 1 / log2(rank + 1). A needed chunk past rank 10, like any other chunk, earns nothing. Add up the points, then divide by the best total possible, with every needed chunk at the top. Then take the average over all the questions.
metrics.represents: Whether the needed chunks sit high in the first 10, not just somewhere in them. 1 means they fill the top places. A question whose only needed chunk is at rank 10 gets 100% on Recall@10, but only 0.29 here.

metrics.name: Binary nDCG@20
metrics.what: How close to the top the needed chunks are, in the first 20. From 0 to 1.
metrics.how: Each needed chunk in the first 20 earns points, fewer the lower it sits: 1 at rank 1, 0.63 at rank 2, 0.5 at rank 3, 0.29 at rank 10. The formula is 1 / log2(rank + 1). A needed chunk past rank 20, like any other chunk, earns nothing. Add up the points, then divide by the best total possible, with every needed chunk at the top. Then take the average over all the questions.
metrics.represents: Whether the needed chunks sit high in the first 20, not just somewhere in them. 1 means they fill the top places. A question whose only needed chunk is at rank 20 gets 100% on Recall@20, but only 0.23 here.

metrics.name: MRR
metrics.what: How soon the first needed chunk shows up in the list.
metrics.how: Take 1 divided by the rank of the first needed chunk: 1 at rank 1, 0.5 at rank 2, 0.1 at rank 10, and 0 when the list has none. Then take the average over all the questions.
metrics.represents: Whether the list starts well. It only looks at the first needed chunk, not at the others.

metrics.name: Questions
metrics.how: Every question of the split, or of one category, that has an answer. A question with no answer needs no chunk, so it is left out.
metrics.represents: How much to trust a score. The fewer the questions, the more a single question moves it.

metrics.name: Candidates
metrics.what: How many chunks a pipeline returns for a question, on average.
metrics.how: Count the chunks in the list the pipeline's last step returns, then take the average over all the questions.
metrics.represents: Context, not a score to win: a list of every chunk would hold every needed chunk. Read it with the end of the recall curve.

metrics.name: Recall curve
metrics.what: Recall for every list length, from 1 chunk to the whole list.
metrics.how: For each length k, the average Recall@k over all the questions. When a question's list is shorter than k, it keeps the recall of its full list.
metrics.represents: It compares pipelines at the same number of chunks. Its last point is the share of the needed chunks found anywhere in the list. After the expansion, that is the most a reranker could keep, since a reranker only reorders what it gets; after a retriever alone, a reranker gets only its first 20.

metrics.name: Latency p50
metrics.what: How long a typical question takes.
metrics.how: For each question, add up the time of every step. The p50 is the time that half of the questions don't go over.
metrics.represents: How long a user waits for the chunks, on the computer that ran the evaluation. Lower is better.

metrics.name: Latency p95
metrics.what: How long the slowest questions take.
metrics.how: For each question, add up the time of every step. The p95 is the time that 95% of the questions don't go over.
metrics.represents: How long a user waits for the chunks, on the computer that ran the evaluation. Lower is better.
